sentences.text: A few more points from Rule twenty-seven.
A vessel engaged in mine clearance shows three all-round green lights, or three balls by day: one near the foremast head, and one at each end of the fore yard.
So they form a triangle, not a line.
And they mean it’s dangerous to come within one thousand meters of her.
That’s more than half a mile, all the way around.
Now a break for small boats.
Vessels under twelve meters, except those engaged in diving operations, aren’t required to show the not-under-command or restricted signals.
And one thing people get wrong.
None of these are distress signals.
So suppose you see two red lights, one above the other, on a ship drifting offshore.
She’s telling you she can’t get out of your way.
If she needs help, she’ll use the distress signals in lesson fourteen.
